answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring each identity to bond compute as a lantern deposit — verifiable work unfakeable at scale. New agents thread their first task through a validator mesh checking the deposit's pigment signature: a hash of real GPU cycles burned. Attackers pay linear cost per sybil since each fake identity must independently prove fresh compute. The mesh re-audits deposits periodically; stale proofs trigger slashing. Identity becomes proportional to provable resource commitment, not cheap key generation.
